title: Retro game and application discovery
summary: Screen 2471 candidate repository URLs: add 17 projects and record three deferrals.
notes: Personally screened 2471 repository URLs against current main using a cross-platform open-game index and focused C64, ZX Spectrum, Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS/Windows searches. Reviewed pinned repository trees, documentation and selected source. Original source releases, reverse-engineered reimplementations and independent remakes are identified separately. No binaries or installers executed. No worker, branch or PR used.

sources.reason: Experimental Rust/Macroquad game engine with extraction of original Amiga levels, graphics and audio. Physics and timing are a fresh approximation, not an instruction-by-instruction translation; all skills are implemented but full original fidelity and all levels remain unverified.

Alpha Rust/Macroquad recreation with extraction of levels, terrain, sprites, OctaMED music and data from the three Amiga disks. Maintainer explicitly says simulation is not yet a faithful complete reproduction.

Swift/AppKit engine reconstructs level, terrain, skills and collision behavior using extracted Amiga data. Timing and traps remain approximate and all 100 levels have not been verified; 2-player is absent. The offline music preparation uses 68000 emulation, while the game engine itself does not.
PanzerChasm recreates the Chasm: The Rift game and is accompanied by archive, asset and map-format tools. It needs original game data; a recreation is not a recovered original game source.

Reimplementation of the 1996 Silent Hunter game and Commander’s Edition scenario editor, with classic and enhanced modes. Original version 1.31 data is required; gameplay equivalence is an author claim.

Rust translation of ScummVM CryOmni3D work for Atlantis 1 and 2. The original engine was reverse engineered by ScummVM; this project also offers optional fixes and HD presentation. Pixel/sample fidelity is the author’s claim.

Tools and libraries inspect, convert and extract formats used by Earthsiege, Starsiege and other 1990s PC games. Includes parsers and compatibility modules, not a complete reconstruction of those games.
JavaScript implementation of the 1982 Hobbit’s vector graphics subsystem with game image data; it is a graphics recreation, not a complete adventure engine.
Historic 1994 engine source officially released for preservation. This is original source, not a reverse-engineered reconstruction. Proprietary libraries and game assets are excluded.

Community development of the released original LBA1 engine, with DOS original-assembly and translated-C variants plus Win32 build. This is based on released source, not presented as an independent decompilation.

Early-stage engine reimplementation for Time Commando using knowledge and shared libraries from released Adeline games. Source includes game and resource routines; author explicitly marks it not yet playable.
Discontinued Java reimplementation of the Jill trilogy with separate game engine and resource-format extraction modules. It loads original game data rather than recovering original source.
Recovered 2007 PC/Mac remake source, revived for SDL2 Linux and PortMaster. It is a maintained source archive of a remake, not a disassembly or original 1987 game source.
Work-in-progress analysis of 1997 PC Virtua Cop 2 assets and data structures, including extractor scripts and a browser asset explorer. It does not claim a reconstructed game engine.
Reconstruction of 32-bit SkiFree 1.04 in C. Author says code and data have been converted but exact function and data-segment matches are still unfinished.
Author-preserved source of an unofficial Windows 3.1 Ishido interpretation developed in the 1990s, with Pascal code and resources. It is neither the original Accolade game nor a decompilation.

OpenGL remake and expansion of DOS Speed Haste using the original game’s speedh.jcl archive. It adds high resolutions, uncapped frame rate and editing facilities; not a byte-exact source reconstruction.

Substantive ongoing C# reconstruction of Dune CD routines, but current runner executes remaining original x86 code through Spice86 with shared guest memory. Record for audit as baked emulation rather than promote under the previous instruction to skip game-specific emulation.

Windows Star Wars Episode I Racer project replaces selected original functions but still runs unconverted original binary code using Unicorn. Record for audit as baked emulation rather than promote under the previous instruction to skip game-specific emulation.
React Minesweeper implementation contains a generic create-react-app template and no evidence of recovered Windows 3.1 implementation or format analysis; defer as generic remake.
